Handle NULL attribute values correctly in change detection

title: Data Quality Pipeline
scenario: Before loading data into the warehouse, your team runs automated quality checks across customer, order, and payment datasets. Each rule produces a row in a quality results table with the violation count and pass/fail status.
objective: Implement validation rules across `customers`, `orders`, and `payments`, and produce a `quality_results` summary with one row per rule.
requirements: Output exactly one row per quality rule (7 rules total)

invalid_order_status — orders where status not in NEW, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED
negative_payment — payments where amount < 0
null_payment_order_id — payments where order_id IS NULL
duplicate_payment_id — count extra rows beyond distinct payment_id

Merge accepted event state with state_snapshot for entities without accepted events

Use schema-aware union — do not rely on positional column alignment across versions
